=== app.py ===
"""Twilio ConversationRelay voice agent for twilio, generated by unmute.

Do not edit this file: change the package and compile again.

Twilio ConversationRelay does the listening and the speaking. This app answers
the voice webhook with TwiML, holds the ConversationRelay WebSocket, thinks with
OpenAI Chat Completions and runs the package's local tools.

  https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/connect/conversationrelay
  https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/conversationrelay/websocket-messages
"""

import asyncio
import inspect
import json
import logging
import os
import re
import threading
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated, Any, Literal
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from aiohttp import WSMsgType, web
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from pydantic import AfterValidator, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, ValidationError, create_model
from twilio.request_validator import RequestValidator


log = logging.getLogger("relay")

# --- compiled settings ---------------------------------------------------------

MODEL = "gpt-5.6-luna"
# Forwarded to every request verbatim, as the package wrote them.
MODEL_PARAMS: dict[str, Any] = json.loads("{\"reasoning_effort\":\"none\"}")
INSTRUCTIONS = "You answer the phone for a front desk. When the caller is done, call end_call.\n"
# ConversationRelay speaks this line itself (welcomeGreeting). The app records it
# in history once and never sends it.
GREETING: str | None = "Hello & welcome, say \"desk\" to start."
TOOL_SPECS: list[dict[str, Any]] = json.loads("[{\"name\":\"end_call\",\"description\":\"End the call once the caller says they are done.\",\"input\":null,\"output\":null,\"end_call\":true}]")

ENV_ACCOUNT_SID = "TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID"
ENV_AUTH_TOKEN = "TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN"
ENV_PUBLIC_URL = "TWILIO_PUBLIC_URL"
ENV_MODEL_KEY = "OPENAI_API_KEY"

# Limits. Each one bounds something a caller or a provider could otherwise grow.
MAX_SESSIONS = 2  # capacity.max_sessions: calls held at once
MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 8  # model and tool round trips per caller turn
TOOL_DEADLINE = 30.0  # seconds a turn waits for one tool
MODEL_TIMEOUT = 30.0  # seconds for one model response
SETUP_TIMEOUT = 10.0  # seconds from WebSocket open to the setup message
DRAIN_TIMEOUT = 20.0  # seconds shutdown waits for calls to finish
END_GRACE = 5.0  # seconds Twilio has to close the socket after an end message
MAX_PENDING_PROMPTS = 8  # caller turns waiting while a tool runs
MAX_PROMPT_CHARS = 4000
MAX_HISTORY = 80  # history entries kept per call
MAX_WS_MESSAGE = 64 * 1024
MAX_RELAY_ERRORS = 5  # ConversationRelay error messages before the call ends
MAX_UNEXPECTED = 20  # unknown or disabled events before the call ends
MAX_FAILURES = 3  # failed model responses in a row before the call ends
FAILURE_LINE = "Sorry, something went wrong on my side. Could you say that again?"

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ORIGIN_PLACEHOLDER = "__PUBLIC_ORIGIN__"
WSS_PLACEHOLDER = "__PUBLIC_WSS_ORIGIN__"
CALL_SID = re.compile(r"CA[0-9a-f]{32}")
SESSION_ID = re.compile(r"VX[0-9a-f]{32}")
HANGUP_TWIML = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><Response><Hangup/></Response>'
# Which build this is, served on /healthz so `unmute deploy` can refuse to route
# a number at a different one. An Unmute drift check, not a Twilio API and not
# an attestation. Hashed from the rest of this file, the TwiML, the pins, the
# image and the tools; never from a credential or the public origin.
ARTIFACT_ID = "sha256:14b26c0ec0cf96de053e9966c42a2bd53678b7feb9e7aa22436ce0d9ec4b931e"

# --- tools ---------------------------------------------------------------------

_JSON_TYPES: dict[str, type] = {"string": str, "integer": int, "number": float, "boolean": bool}


def one_of(values: list[Any]) -> Any:
    def check(value: Any) -> Any:
        if value not in values:
            raise ValueError(f"must be one of {values}")
        return value

    return AfterValidator(check)


def schema_model(
    name: str, schema: dict[str, Any] | None, extra: Literal["allow", "forbid"]
) -> type[BaseModel] | None:
    """Lower a flat object schema of primitive fields to a Pydantic model.

    unmute refuses any other schema at compile time, so nothing else reaches
    here. Fields are aliased, so a property named like a BaseModel attribute
    still works.
    """
    if schema is None:
        return None
    required = set(schema.get("required", []))
    fields: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for index, (key, prop) in enumerate(schema.get("properties", {}).items()):
        annotation: Any = _JSON_TYPES[prop["type"]]
        if "enum" in prop:
            annotation = Annotated[annotation, one_of(prop["enum"])]
        if key in required:
            fields[f"f{index}"] = (annotation, Field(alias=key))
        else:
            fields[f"f{index}"] = (annotation | None, Field(default=None, alias=key))
    return create_model(name, __config__=ConfigDict(extra=extra), **fields)


@dataclass
class Tool:
    name: str
    declaration: dict[str, Any]
    args: type[BaseModel] | None
    result: type[BaseModel] | None
    run: Any  # the handler, or None for end_call
    end_call: bool


HANDLERS: dict[str, Any] = {
}


def load_tools() -> dict[str, Tool]:
    loaded = {}
    for spec in TOOL_SPECS:
        parameters = spec["input"] or {"type": "object", "properties": {}}
        output = spec["output"]
        extra = "forbid" if output and output.get("additionalProperties") is False else "allow"
        loaded[spec["name"]] = Tool(
            name=spec["name"],
            declaration={"name": spec["name"], "description": spec["description"], "parameters": parameters},
            # Arguments never take an undeclared key, whatever the schema says.
            args=schema_model(spec["name"] + "_args", parameters, "forbid"),
            result=schema_model(spec["name"] + "_result", output, extra),
            run=None if spec["end_call"] else HANDLERS[spec["name"]],
            end_call=spec["end_call"],
        )
    return loaded


TOOLS = load_tools()


def settle(future: asyncio.Future, value: Any, error: BaseException | None) -> None:
    if future.done():
        return
    if error is not None:
        future.set_exception(error)
    else:
        future.set_result(value)


def start_handler(run: Any, kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> asyncio.Future:
    """Start a handler without tying it to the caller's turn.

    An async handler runs as a task. A sync handler runs in a daemon thread,
    so a hung one cannot block process exit or queue behind another call's.
    Neither is ever cancelled: a thread cannot be stopped, and cancelling a
    task mid-action could leave an action half done. Bound your own I/O.
    """
    if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(run):
        return asyncio.ensure_future(run(**kwargs))
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    future = loop.create_future()

    def work() -> None:
        try:
            value, error = run(**kwargs), None
        except BaseException as caught:  # noqa: BLE001 - handed to the loop as the outcome
            value, error = None, caught
        try:
            loop.call_soon_threadsafe(settle, future, value, error)
        except RuntimeError:
            pass  # the loop closed while the handler ran: the process is exiting

    threading.Thread(target=work, name="tool", daemon=True).start()
    return future


# --- the model -----------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass
class ToolCall:
    id: str
    name: str
    arguments: Any  # a JSON string


@dataclass
class Reply:
    calls: list[ToolCall]
    generated: str  # every text fragment the model produced, spoken or not
    raw: Any = None  # the provider's own parts, kept for the history


@dataclass
class Cycle:
    """One speech cycle: the text between two last=true markers."""

    generation: int
    held: str | None = None  # the newest fragment, held so last=true can ride it
    sent: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # fragments handed to the socket
    done: bool = False
    entry: Any = None  # the history entry holding this cycle's text

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        return "".join(self.sent)


def make_client() -> AsyncOpenAI:
    # No SDK retries: a retry would spend the caller's silence. A failed
    # response takes the failure path instead.
    return AsyncOpenAI(api_key=os.environ[ENV_MODEL_KEY], max_retries=0, timeout=MODEL_TIMEOUT)


class Brain:
    """Chat Completions history for one call.

    https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat
    """

    def __init__(self, client: Any) -> None:
        self.client = client
        self.history: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.tools = [{"type": "function", "function": tool.declaration} for tool in TOOLS.values()]

    def user(self, text: str) -> None:
        self.history.append({"role": "user", "content": text})

    def assistant_text(self, text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        entry = {"role": "assistant", "content": text}
        self.history.append(entry)
        return entry

    async def stream(self, call: "Call", cycle: Cycle) -> Reply:
        request: dict[str, Any] = {
            "model": MODEL,
            "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": INSTRUCTIONS}, *self.history],
            "stream": True,
            **MODEL_PARAMS,
        }
        if self.tools:
            request["tools"] = self.tools
        slots: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {}
        generated: list[str] = []
        stream = await self.client.chat.completions.create(**request)
        try:
            async for chunk in stream:
                if not chunk.choices:
                    continue
                delta = chunk.choices[0].delta
                if delta.content:
                    generated.append(delta.content)
                    await call.speak(cycle, delta.content)
                for part in delta.tool_calls or []:
                    slot = slots.setdefault(part.index, {"id": "", "name": "", "arguments": ""})
                    slot["id"] = part.id or slot["id"]
                    if part.function is not None:
                        slot["name"] += part.function.name or ""
                        slot["arguments"] += part.function.arguments or ""
        finally:
            await stream.close()
        calls = [ToolCall(s["id"], s["name"], s["arguments"]) for _, s in sorted(slots.items())]
        return Reply(calls=calls, generated="".join(generated))

    def commit(self, cycle: Cycle, reply: Reply, results: list[tuple[ToolCall, Any]]) -> Any:
        entry: dict[str, Any] = {"role": "assistant", "content": cycle.text or None}
        if reply.calls:
            entry["tool_calls"] = [
                {"id": c.id, "type": "function", "function": {"name": c.name, "arguments": valid_json(c.arguments)}}
                for c in reply.calls
            ]
        elif not cycle.text:
            return None
        self.history.append(entry)
        for tool_call, result in results:
            self.history.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tool_call.id, "content": json.dumps(result)})
        return entry

    def set_text(self, entry: Any, text: str) -> None:
        if text:
            entry["content"] = text
        elif entry.get("tool_calls"):
            entry["content"] = None
        else:
            remove_entry(self.history, entry)

    def trim(self) -> None:
        trim_history(self.history, lambda e: e["role"] == "user")


def valid_json(arguments: Any) -> str:
    # Replayed to the model as sent, unless it is not JSON at all: the tool
    # result already says the arguments were refused.
    try:
        json.loads(arguments)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return "{}"
    return arguments


def remove_entry(history: list[Any], entry: Any) -> None:
    for index, item in enumerate(history):
        if item is entry:
            del history[index]
            return


def trim_history(history: list[Any], is_user_turn: Any) -> None:
    """Drop the oldest turns, cutting only where a caller turn starts, so a
    tool call is never separated from its result."""
    if len(history) <= MAX_HISTORY:
        return
    for index in range(len(history) - MAX_HISTORY, len(history)):
        if is_user_turn(history[index]):
            del history[:index]
            return


# --- one call ------------------------------------------------------------------


class Call:
    """One ConversationRelay session.

    Two coroutines share it. The reader takes messages off the socket and
    never waits on the model. The owner is the only writer of the history. A
    generation number tags speech: an interrupt or a new caller turn bumps it,
    and every send checks it under one lock, so a late fragment from the old
    generation is dropped at the last moment it could still be stopped. Bytes
    already sent cannot be recalled; ConversationRelay decides what it plays.
    """

    def __init__(self, ws: web.WebSocketResponse, setup: dict[str, Any], client: Any, slots: "Slots") -> None:
        self.ws = ws
        self.call_sid = setup["callSid"]
        self.session_id = setup["sessionId"]
        self.brain = Brain(client)
        self.slots = slots
        self.generation = 0
        self.send_lock = asyncio.Lock()
        self.pending: list[str] = []
        self.interrupt: str | None = None
        self.wake = asyncio.Event()
        self.stream_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self.cycle: Cycle | None = None
        self.spoken: Cycle | None = None  # the last cycle that reached the socket
        self.tool_future: asyncio.Future | None = None
        self.failures = 0
        self.relay_errors = 0
        self.unexpected = 0
        self.ending = False
        self.closed = False
        self.closer: asyncio.Task | None = None  # closes the socket if Twilio does not
        self.holding = False  # the slot outlives the call until a handler ends
        self.released = False
        if GREETING:
            greeting = Cycle(generation=0, sent=[GREETING], done=True)
            greeting.entry = self.brain.assistant_text(GREETING)
            self.spoken = greeting

    def event(self, name: str, **fields: Any) -> None:
        details = " ".join(f"{key}={value}" for key, value in fields.items())
        log.info("event=%s call=%s session=%s %s", name, self.call_sid, self.session_id, details)

    # --- sending ---------------------------------------------------------------

    async def send_token(self, cycle: Cycle, token: str, last: bool, force: bool = False) -> None:
        async with self.send_lock:
            if self.closed or (cycle.generation != self.generation and not force):
                return
            # Recorded before the await: once the send starts, the text may
            # reach ConversationRelay even if this coroutine is cancelled.
            cycle.sent.append(token)
            self.spoken = cycle
            try:
                await self.ws.send_json({"type": "text", "token": token, "last": last})
            except (ConnectionError, RuntimeError):
                # The peer is gone. Nothing more can be said on this call,
                # and the reader is about to see the close.
                self.closed = True

    async def speak(self, cycle: Cycle, fragment: str) -> None:
        if not fragment:
            return
        previous, cycle.held = cycle.held, fragment
        if previous is not None:
            await self.send_token(cycle, previous, last=False)

    async def finish(self, cycle: Cycle) -> None:
        """Send the held fragment with last=true, closing the cycle."""
        fragment, cycle.held = cycle.held, None
        if fragment is not None:
            await self.send_token(cycle, fragment, last=True)
        cycle.done = True

    async def say_fixed(self, text: str) -> None:
        cycle = Cycle(generation=self.generation)
        self.cycle = cycle
        await self.speak(cycle, text)
        await self.finish(cycle)
        if cycle.sent:
            cycle.entry = self.brain.assistant_text(cycle.text)

    async def end(self, reason: str) -> None:
        """Hand the call back to Twilio, which then requests /connect-action."""
        if self.closed:
            return
        self.event("end", reason=reason)
        async with self.send_lock:
            self.closed = True
            try:
                await self.ws.send_json({"type": "end", "handoffData": json.dumps({"reasonCode": reason})})
            except ConnectionError:
                pass
        # Twilio closes the socket once it has taken the end message. Closing
        # it here first can reach Twilio before the end does, and the session
        # then fails as 64105 "WebSocket ended" instead of ending. The reader
        # keeps draining until Twilio closes; this closes only for a peer that
        # never does.
        self.closer = asyncio.ensure_future(self.close_after(END_GRACE))

    async def close_after(self, seconds: float) -> None:
        await asyncio.sleep(seconds)
        await self.ws.close()

    # --- the reader --------------------------------------------------------------

    async def read(self) -> None:
        async for message in self.ws:
            if self.closed:
                # The call has ended on our side. Only Twilio's close is left.
                continue
            if message.type != WSMsgType.TEXT:
                self.event("protocol_error", detail="non_text_frame")
                await self.ws.close(code=1003)
                return
            try:
                event = json.loads(message.data)
            except ValueError:
                event = None
            if not isinstance(event, dict):
                self.event("protocol_error", detail="malformed_json")
                await self.ws.close(code=1007)
                return
            kind = event.get("type")
            if kind == "prompt":
                # Partial transcripts start nothing: only a final one is a turn.
                text = event.get("voicePrompt")
                if event.get("last") is not True or not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
                    continue
                if len(self.pending) >= MAX_PENDING_PROMPTS:
                    await self.end("prompt_overflow")
                    continue
                await self.on_prompt(text[:MAX_PROMPT_CHARS])
            elif kind == "interrupt":
                heard = event.get("utteranceUntilInterrupt")
                self.on_interrupt(heard if isinstance(heard, str) else "")
            elif kind == "error":
                self.relay_errors += 1
                self.event("relay_error", count=self.relay_errors)
                if self.relay_errors >= MAX_RELAY_ERRORS:
                    await self.end("relay_errors")
            else:
                # dtmf is disabled in the TwiML, a second setup is a protocol
                # error, and anything else is not ours to act on.
                self.unexpected += 1
                self.event("unexpected_event", kind=str(kind)[:32])
                if kind == "setup" or self.unexpected >= MAX_UNEXPECTED:
                    await self.end("protocol_error")

    async def on_prompt(self, text: str) -> None:
        # Each final prompt is its own turn, kept as said: two identical
        # sentences are two things the caller said.
        self.pending.append(text)
        cycle = self.cycle
        self.generation += 1
        self.cancel_stream()
        if cycle is not None and not cycle.done and cycle.held is not None:
            # Close ConversationRelay's open utterance before the next one.
            fragment, cycle.held = cycle.held, None
            await self.send_token(cycle, fragment, last=True, force=True)
            cycle.done = True
        self.wake.set()

    def on_interrupt(self, heard: str) -> None:
        self.generation += 1
        self.cancel_stream()
        if self.cycle is not None:
            self.cycle.held = None  # never sent, and now never will be
        self.interrupt = heard
        self.wake.set()

    def cancel_stream(self) -> None:
        # Only the model stream is cancellable. A running tool is not touched.
        if self.stream_task is not None and not self.stream_task.done():
            self.stream_task.cancel()

    # --- the owner ---------------------------------------------------------------

    async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            while not self.closed:
                await self.wake.wait()
                self.wake.clear()
                self.reconcile()
                if self.pending:
                    await self.respond()
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - a dead owner would leave the caller in silence
            self.event("owner_failed", error=type(error).__name__)
            await self.end("internal_error")

    def take_pending(self) -> None:
        for text in self.pending:
            self.brain.user(text)
        self.pending.clear()
        # A new caller turn closes the old cycle to reconciliation.
        self.spoken = None
        self.brain.trim()

    def reconcile(self) -> None:
        """Cut the interrupted cycle's history down to what the caller heard.

        Only the last cycle that reached the socket is touched. If the heard
        text is not a clear prefix of what was sent, the cycle's text is
        dropped rather than guessed at. Earlier turns and tool results are
        never edited.
        """
        cycle = self.spoken
        if self.interrupt is None or cycle is None:
            self.interrupt = None
            return
        if cycle.entry is None:
            return  # its text is not in the history yet; the owner comes back
        heard, self.interrupt = self.interrupt, None
        self.spoken = None
        kept = heard_prefix(cycle.text, heard)
        if kept != cycle.text:
            self.brain.set_text(cycle.entry, kept)
            self.event("interrupted", kept_chars=len(kept), sent_chars=len(cycle.text))

    async def respond(self) -> None:
        self.take_pending()
        rounds = 0
        while not self.closed:
            cycle = Cycle(generation=self.generation)
            self.cycle = cycle
            self.stream_task = asyncio.ensure_future(self.stream(cycle))
            await asyncio.wait({self.stream_task})
            task, self.stream_task = self.stream_task, None
            if task.cancelled():
                # An interrupt or a new caller turn. Keep what was really sent.
                cycle.entry = self.brain.commit(cycle, Reply(calls=[], generated=cycle.text), [])
                self.reconcile()
                return
            if task.exception() is not None:
                await self.fail(cycle, type(task.exception()).__name__)
                return
            reply = task.result()
            await self.finish(cycle)
            if not reply.calls and not cycle.sent and not reply.generated:
                await self.fail(cycle, "empty_response")
                return
            self.failures = 0
            if not reply.calls:
                cycle.entry = self.brain.commit(cycle, reply, [])
                self.reconcile()
                return
            rounds += 1
            results = await self.run_tools(reply.calls)
            # A duplicated call id ran once, so it is answered once and kept
            # once: a call turn with an unanswered call is refused next turn.
            reply.calls = [tool_call for tool_call, _ in results]
            # The call turn and its results enter the history together, so the
            # history is valid for the provider at every point.
            cycle.entry = self.brain.commit(cycle, reply, results)
            self.reconcile()
            if self.ending:
                await self.end("end_call")
                return
            if self.pending:
                self.take_pending()
            if rounds >= MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS:
                self.event("tool_rounds_exhausted", rounds=rounds)
                await self.say_fixed(FAILURE_LINE)
                return
            # The next round takes the current generation, so an interrupt
            # during the tool does not silence the answer that uses its result.

    async def stream(self, cycle: Cycle) -> Reply:
        async with asyncio.timeout(MODEL_TIMEOUT):
            return await self.brain.stream(self, cycle)

    async def fail(self, cycle: Cycle, reason: str) -> None:
        self.failures += 1
        self.event("model_failed", reason=reason, count=self.failures)
        # Whatever was already said stays said.
        if cycle.sent:
            await self.finish(cycle)
            cycle.entry = self.brain.assistant_text(cycle.text)
        if self.failures >= MAX_FAILURES:
            await self.end("model_failures")
            return
        await self.say_fixed(FAILURE_LINE)

    # --- tools -------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def run_tools(self, calls: list[ToolCall]) -> list[tuple[ToolCall, Any]]:
        results = []
        seen = set()
        for tool_call in calls:
            key = tool_call.id or f"{tool_call.name}:{len(results)}"
            if key in seen:
                continue  # a duplicated call id runs once
            seen.add(key)
            results.append((tool_call, await self.run_tool(tool_call)))
        return results

    async def run_tool(self, tool_call: ToolCall) -> Any:
        tool = TOOLS.get(tool_call.name)
        if tool is None:
            self.event("tool_unknown")
            return {"error": "unknown_tool", "detail": "no tool with that name"}
        if tool.end_call:
            self.ending = True
            return {"ok": True}
        arguments = tool_call.arguments
        if isinstance(arguments, str):
            try:
                arguments = json.loads(arguments or "{}")
            except ValueError:
                return {"error": "invalid_arguments", "detail": "arguments are not JSON"}
        if not isinstance(arguments, dict):
            return {"error": "invalid_arguments", "detail": "arguments must be an object"}
        try:
            parsed = tool.args.model_validate(arguments) if tool.args else None
        except ValidationError as error:
            problems = [{"field": ".".join(map(str, e["loc"])), "problem": e["type"]} for e in error.errors()]
            return {"error": "invalid_arguments", "detail": problems}
        if self.tool_future is not None and not self.tool_future.done():
            return {"error": "busy", "detail": "an earlier action is still running and its outcome is unknown"}
        kwargs = parsed.model_dump(by_alias=True, exclude_unset=True) if parsed else {}
        future = start_handler(tool.run, kwargs)
        self.tool_future = future
        future.add_done_callback(lambda done: self.tool_settled(tool.name, done))
        self.event("tool_started", tool=tool.name)
        finished, _ = await asyncio.wait({future}, timeout=TOOL_DEADLINE)
        if not finished:
            # Still running, and it keeps running. Say so rather than guess.
            self.event("tool_timeout", tool=tool.name)
            return {"error": "timeout", "outcome": "unknown", "detail": "the action did not finish in time; it may still complete"}
        if future.exception() is not None:
            self.event("tool_failed", tool=tool.name, error=type(future.exception()).__name__)
            return {"error": "tool_failed", "detail": "the action raised an error"}
        result = future.result()
        try:
            if tool.result is not None:
                tool.result.model_validate(result)
            json.dumps(result)
        except (ValidationError, TypeError, ValueError):
            self.event("tool_bad_result", tool=tool.name)
            return {"error": "invalid_result", "detail": "the action returned something its declared output does not allow"}
        return result

    def tool_settled(self, name: str, future: asyncio.Future) -> None:
        if not future.cancelled() and future.exception() is not None:
            future.exception()  # retrieved, so asyncio does not log it as lost
        if self.holding:
            self.holding = False
            self.event("tool_finished_after_call", tool=name)
            self.slots.orphaned -= 1
            self.release()

    # --- ending ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def close(self) -> None:
        """The socket is gone. Give the slot back once no handler is running."""
        self.closed = True
        self.cancel_stream()
        if self.closer is not None:
            self.closer.cancel()
        if self.tool_future is not None and not self.tool_future.done():
            self.holding = True
            self.slots.orphaned += 1
            self.event("slot_held", reason="tool_still_running")
            return
        self.release()

    def release(self) -> None:
        if not self.released:
            self.released = True
            self.slots.give_back()


async def drain(ws: web.WebSocketResponse) -> None:
    """Read and drop messages until the peer closes the socket."""
    async for _ in ws:
        pass


def heard_prefix(sent: str, heard: str) -> str:
    """The part of `sent` the caller heard, or "" when that is not clear."""

    def norm(text: str) -> str:
        return " ".join(text.split()).lower()

    target = norm(heard)
    if not target or not norm(sent).startswith(target):
        return ""
    for end in range(len(sent) + 1):
        if len(norm(sent[:end])) >= len(target):
            return sent[:end]
    return sent


# --- the web app ---------------------------------------------------------------


class Slots:
    """Bounded call admission. One process, so a counter is the whole story."""

    def __init__(self, limit: int) -> None:
        self.limit = limit
        self.taken = 0
        self.orphaned = 0  # held by calls that ended while a handler still runs
        self.draining = False
        self.idle = asyncio.Event()
        self.idle.set()

    def has_room(self) -> bool:
        return not self.draining and self.taken < self.limit

    def take(self) -> bool:
        if not self.has_room():
            return False
        self.taken += 1
        self.idle.clear()
        return True

    def give_back(self) -> None:
        self.taken -= 1
        if self.taken == 0:
            self.idle.set()


def public_origin(value: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Read the public URL as an https origin. Everything signed is built from
    it, never from request headers, because a proxy can rewrite those."""
    parts = urlsplit(value.strip())
    if (
        parts.scheme != "https"
        or not parts.hostname
        or parts.username
        or parts.password
        or parts.path not in ("", "/")
        or parts.query
        or parts.fragment
    ):
        raise SystemExit(
            f"{ENV_PUBLIC_URL} must be an https origin with no path, query or credentials, "
            "for example https://relay.example.com"
        )
    return f"https://{parts.netloc}", parts.netloc


def render_twiml(origin: str, host: str) -> str:
    root = ET.parse(HERE / "conversation-relay.xml.tmpl").getroot()
    connect = root.find("Connect")
    relay = connect.find("ConversationRelay") if connect is not None else None
    if connect is None or relay is None:
        raise SystemExit("conversation-relay.xml.tmpl has no Connect/ConversationRelay element")
    connect.set("action", origin + "/connect-action")
    relay.set("url", f"wss://{host}/conversation")
    body = ET.tostring(root, encoding="unicode")
    if ORIGIN_PLACEHOLDER in body or WSS_PLACEHOLDER in body:
        raise SystemExit("conversation-relay.xml.tmpl still carries a placeholder after rendering")
    return '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>' + body


def xml_response(body: str) -> web.Response:
    return web.Response(text=body, content_type="text/xml")


def build_app(client: Any = None) -> web.Application:
    missing = [name for name in (ENV_ACCOUNT_SID, ENV_AUTH_TOKEN, ENV_PUBLIC_URL, ENV_MODEL_KEY) if not os.environ.get(name)]
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit("missing environment: " + ", ".join(missing))
    account_sid = os.environ[ENV_ACCOUNT_SID]
    validator = RequestValidator(os.environ[ENV_AUTH_TOKEN])
    origin, host = public_origin(os.environ[ENV_PUBLIC_URL])
    twiml = render_twiml(origin, host)
    slots = Slots(MAX_SESSIONS)
    calls: set[Call] = set()
    model_client = client or make_client()

    def signed(request: web.Request, urls: list[str], params: Any) -> bool:
        signature = request.headers.get("X-Twilio-Signature", "")
        return bool(signature) and any(validator.validate(url, params, signature) for url in urls)

    async def healthz(request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        # 503 while draining, or when every slot is held by a handler that
        # outlived its call: the process can take no call either way. A 200
        # does not promise a free slot: /voice may still answer <Hangup/>.
        if slots.draining or slots.orphaned >= slots.limit:
            return web.json_response({"ok": False, "artifact_id": ARTIFACT_ID}, status=503)
        return web.json_response({"ok": True, "artifact_id": ARTIFACT_ID})

    async def voice(request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        # https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/security: the exact URL Twilio
        # requested, query included, plus every form field.
        form = await request.post()
        if not signed(request, [origin + request.raw_path], form):
            log.warning("event=signature_rejected route=/voice")
            raise web.HTTPForbidden()
        if form.get("AccountSid") != account_sid:
            log.warning("event=account_rejected route=/voice")
            raise web.HTTPForbidden()
        if not slots.has_room():
            log.info("event=call_refused reason=%s", "draining" if slots.draining else "full")
            return xml_response(HANGUP_TWIML)
        return xml_response(twiml)

    async def connect_action(request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        # https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/connect: Twilio asks here what
        # to do once the session ends. HandoffData is ignored: this app hands
        # the call to nobody. The answer is always to hang up.
        form = await request.post()
        if not signed(request, [origin + request.raw_path], form):
            log.warning("event=signature_rejected route=/connect-action")
            raise web.HTTPForbidden()
        if form.get("AccountSid") != account_sid:
            raise web.HTTPForbidden()
        log.info(
            "event=session_ended call=%s status=%s error=%s",
            str(form.get("CallSid", ""))[:34],
            str(form.get("SessionStatus", ""))[:16],
            str(form.get("ErrorCode", ""))[:8],
        )
        return xml_response(HANGUP_TWIML)

    async def conversation(request: web.Request) -> web.StreamResponse:
        # The handshake is signed over the wss URL with no form fields. Twilio
        # documents one variant: a trailing slash on the path.
        path, _, query = request.raw_path.partition("?")
        suffix = "?" + query if query else ""
        urls = [f"wss://{host}{path}{suffix}", f"wss://{host}{path}/{suffix}"]
        if not signed(request, urls, {}):
            log.warning("event=signature_rejected route=/conversation")
            raise web.HTTPForbidden()
        ws = web.WebSocketResponse(max_msg_size=MAX_WS_MESSAGE)
        await ws.prepare(request)
        try:
            first = await asyncio.wait_for(ws.receive(), SETUP_TIMEOUT)
            setup = json.loads(first.data) if first.type == WSMsgType.TEXT else None
        except (TimeoutError, ValueError):
            setup = None
        if (
            not isinstance(setup, dict)
            or setup.get("type") != "setup"
            or setup.get("accountSid") != account_sid
            or not CALL_SID.fullmatch(str(setup.get("callSid", "")))
            or not SESSION_ID.fullmatch(str(setup.get("sessionId", "")))
        ):
            log.warning("event=setup_rejected")
            await ws.close(code=1008)
            return ws
        # Call state starts here, after the setup message proved the account.
        if not slots.take():
            log.info("event=call_refused reason=%s", "draining" if slots.draining else "full")
            await ws.send_json({"type": "end", "handoffData": json.dumps({"reasonCode": "busy"})})
            # As in Call.end: wait for Twilio to close, or the refusal fails as 64105.
            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(drain(ws), END_GRACE)
            except TimeoutError:
                pass
            await ws.close()
            return ws
        call = Call(ws, setup, model_client, slots)
        calls.add(call)
        call.event("call_started", direction=str(setup.get("direction", ""))[:16])
        owner = asyncio.ensure_future(call.run())
        try:
            await call.read()
        finally:
            # Synchronous first: aiohttp may cancel this handler when the peer
            # goes away, and the slot must be accounted for either way.
            call.close()
            calls.discard(call)
            owner.cancel()
            call.event("call_closed")
        await asyncio.gather(owner, return_exceptions=True)
        return ws

    async def on_shutdown(app: web.Application) -> None:
        # Stop taking calls, give the current ones a bounded time, then end
        # whatever is left.
        slots.draining = True
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(slots.idle.wait(), DRAIN_TIMEOUT)
        except TimeoutError:
            pass
        for call in list(calls):
            await call.end("shutdown")

    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_get("/healthz", healthz)
    app.router.add_post("/voice", voice)
    app.router.add_post("/connect-action", connect_action)
    app.router.add_get("/conversation", conversation)
    app.on_shutdown.append(on_shutdown)
    return app


def main() -> None:
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
    web.run_app(
        build_app(),
        host="0.0.0.0",
        port=int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8080")),
        shutdown_timeout=DRAIN_TIMEOUT + 5,
        access_log=None,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# One process, as a non-root user. The app terminates HTTPS nowhere: put it
# behind a proxy or platform that serves your public https origin.
FROM python:3.12-slim

RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && useradd --create-home --uid 10001 relay

WORKDIR /app
COPY pyproject.toml ./
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir uv \
    && uv pip install --system --no-cache -r pyproject.toml

COPY app.py conversation-relay.xml.tmpl ./

USER relay
ENV PORT=8080 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["python", "app.py"]

=== README.md ===
# twilio

A Twilio ConversationRelay voice agent, generated by unmute. Do not edit these
files: change the package and run `unmute compile` again.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller
    participant Twilio
    participant App as app.py
    participant Model as OpenAI
    Caller->>Twilio: calls your number
    Twilio->>App: POST /voice (signed)
    App-->>Twilio: TwiML: Connect + ConversationRelay
    Twilio->>App: WebSocket /conversation (signed)
    Twilio->>App: caller speech as text
    App->>Model: history + tools
    Model-->>App: streamed reply
    App-->>Twilio: text tokens
    Twilio-->>Caller: speech
    Twilio->>App: POST /connect-action when the session ends
    App-->>Twilio: Hangup
```

1. Twilio answers the call and asks `/voice` what to do.
2. The app answers with TwiML that connects the call to ConversationRelay.
3. ConversationRelay opens a WebSocket to `/conversation`. It turns the
   caller's speech into text and the app's text into speech.
4. The app sends the conversation to the model, runs any tool the model asks
   for, and streams the reply back as text.
5. To end the session, the app sends `end` and waits up to five seconds for
   Twilio to close the WebSocket. Closing it first can fail the session with
   [error 64105](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/64105). Twilio then asks `/connect-action`,
   and the app hangs up.

## What is in this folder

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `app.py` | The whole app: HTTP routes, the WebSocket, the model, the tools. |
| `conversation-relay.xml.tmpl` | The TwiML `/voice` returns. `app.py` fills in your public origin at startup. |
| `pyproject.toml` | Exact dependency pins. |
| `Dockerfile` | A non-root image that runs one process. |
| `.env.example` | Every environment name `app.py` reads. |
| `compile-report.json` | What was resolved, the pins, and what is and is not verified. |

## Run it

You host this app yourself. unmute never uploads it, never buys a number and
never places a call. The one thing it can change in your Twilio account is the
voice webhook of one number you name, and only when you run `unmute deploy`.

1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill it in.
2. Start the app on your host:

   ```sh
   uv run --env-file .env python app.py
   ```

   Or build the image:

   ```sh
   docker build -t twilio-relay .
   docker run --env-file .env -p 8080:8080 twilio-relay
   ```

3. Point Twilio at it. These steps are the route's own, word for word
   ([ConversationRelay onboarding](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/conversationrelay/onboarding),
   [phone numbers](https://www.twilio.com/docs/phone-numbers)):

   - host the built app behind HTTPS at a public origin you control, and set the public_url environment name to that origin, for example https://relay.example.com, with no path
   - take the number off any SIP trunk and any TwiML App, and clear its voice fallback URL: deploy refuses a number with any of them, and never clears one for you
   - run `unmute deploy --target <name> --dry-run`, then again without --dry-run, to point the number at https://<your origin>/voice; or, in the Twilio Console, open the number (Phone Numbers, Manage, Active Numbers) and set "A call comes in" to Webhook, HTTP POST, https://<your origin>/voice

   Twilio must reach `/voice`, `/conversation` and `/connect-action` at your
   origin. `TWILIO_PUBLIC_URL` is the environment name for that origin.
4. Call the number.

`GET /healthz` answers 200 while the process is up, even when every call slot
is busy: then `/voice` answers `<Hangup/>`. It answers 503 only while the app
drains, or when every slot is held by a tool handler that outlived its call.
Both answers carry `artifact_id`, the build this app is.

## Point the number with unmute deploy

`unmute deploy --target twilio` sets the number's webhook for you. Run it
where the package is, after step 2. It reads these environment names, from the
shell or the package's `.env`:

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` | The account that owns the number. |
| `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` | That account's Auth Token. It must be the one the host uses. |
| `TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER_SID` | The number to route, `PN` followed by 32 characters. Only deploy reads it. |
| `TWILIO_PUBLIC_URL` | The host's public origin, the same value the host has. |

It needs no model key: the model runs on your host. It then does this, in order:

1. Reads the number
   ([IncomingPhoneNumber](https://www.twilio.com/docs/phone-numbers/api/incomingphonenumber-resource)). It refuses a number that
   cannot take voice calls, or that has a TwiML App, a SIP trunk or a voice
   fallback URL. It never clears one of those for you.
2. Reads `/healthz` and compares its `artifact_id` with this build. A different
   or missing id means the host runs another build: recompile, rehost, run again.
   The id is unmute's own drift check, not a Twilio feature.
3. Sends `/voice` one request signed with the Auth Token, the way Twilio signs a
   call ([webhook security](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/security)), and compares the TwiML with
   this build's ([Connect](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/connect),
   [ConversationRelay](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/connect/conversationrelay)). This proves the HTTP
   answer only. It does not open the WebSocket, run the model or place a call.
   A 503 or a `<Hangup/>` answer means "busy, try again later".
4. With `--dry-run`, stops here and prints the change it would make. A dry run
   writes no file, not even the report.
5. Stops if the number already points at `https://<your origin>/voice` with
   `POST`.
6. Reads the number again. It stops if the voice settings moved, or if the
   number now fails a check from step 1.
7. Saves the old voice URL and method to a new private file under your user
   config directory, in `unmute/twilio-rollback/`. If that fails, it stops.
8. Sets `VoiceUrl` and `VoiceMethod` only. SMS and every other setting stay as
   they were.
9. Reads the number back. The result is `routed` only if the number points at
   `/voice` with `POST` and still passes every check from step 1. It is
   `not_changed` only if Twilio refused the write. Anything else, such as a
   timeout, is `unknown`, because the write may still land. It writes
   `build/twilio/deploy-report.json` with IDs, the outcome and the snapshot
   path. `call_verified` is always false: only a real call verifies a call.

Two deploys to one number at the same time are not supported.

### Put the old route back

The deploy prints the snapshot path. The file holds the exact old URL, which
may carry a secret, so it is readable only by you.

1. Open the number in the Twilio Console. Check that "A call comes in" is still
   a webhook to the snapshot's `new_voice_url` with `HTTP POST`. Check that the
   number has no TwiML App, no SIP trunk and no fallback URL. If any of this is
   different, somebody changed the number after the deploy: stop, and decide
   with them.
2. Set "A call comes in" back to the snapshot's `voice_url` and `voice_method`.

## How it behaves

- **Signatures.** Every request must carry a valid `X-Twilio-Signature`
  ([Twilio webhook security](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/security)). The app checks it against
  `TWILIO_PUBLIC_URL` plus the exact path and query, never against request
  headers, because a proxy can rewrite those. The WebSocket handshake is checked
  against `wss://<host>/conversation`, and also with a trailing slash, which is
  the one variant Twilio documents. Real proxy behaviour is not verified yet.
- **Calls at once.** At most 2 calls (`capacity.max_sessions`).
  When full, `/voice` answers with `<Hangup/>`. One process, one replica: do
  not run two copies behind one number.
- **Speech.** ConversationRelay does all listening and speaking
  ([attributes](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/connect/conversationrelay)). DTMF detection is off.
  ConversationRelay speaks the greeting itself; the app only records it.
- **Replies.** Each reply is streamed as text tokens
  ([WebSocket messages](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/conversationrelay/websocket-messages)). `last: true` marks the end of one
  reply. It means the app has sent the reply, not that the caller has heard it.
- **Interruptions.** When the caller talks over the agent, the app stops
  sending that reply and keeps in history only the part the caller heard. Text
  already sent to Twilio cannot be recalled by the app.
- **Tools.** Arguments are checked against the tool's input schema before the
  handler runs, and results against its output schema. A tool runs to the end
  and is never cancelled. After 30 seconds the turn moves on and
  the outcome is reported as unknown to the model. A synchronous handler runs
  in its own thread, which Python cannot stop, so bound your handler's own
  network calls. The call slot stays taken until the handler really finishes.
  At most 8 tool rounds per caller turn.
- **Ending the call.** `end_call` ends the session at once, so a goodbye the
  agent says in the same turn may be cut off.
- **Failures.** If the model fails or times out, the agent says one short
  fixed line. After three failures in a row the call ends.
- **Logs.** Call and session IDs, event names and error class names. Never the
  transcript, the prompt, tool arguments or environment values.

## Not verified yet

- A real call through a Twilio number. The protocol is tested offline against
  a signed fake ConversationRelay client.
- The signed WebSocket handshake behind a real proxy.
- How Twilio plays tokens that were already sent when an interrupt arrives.
- Regions other than Twilio's default US1.
=== conversation-relay.xml.tmpl ===
<!-- ConversationRelay TwiML for twilio, generated by unmute. Not final TwiML:
     app.py replaces __PUBLIC_ORIGIN__ and __PUBLIC_WSS_ORIGIN__ with the public origin at startup. -->
<Response>
  <Connect action="__PUBLIC_ORIGIN__/connect-action" method="POST">
    <ConversationRelay url="__PUBLIC_WSS_ORIGIN__/conversation" transcriptionProvider="Deepgram" speechModel="nova-3-general" transcriptionLanguage="en-US" ttsProvider="ElevenLabs" voice="UgBBYS2sOqTuMpoF3BR0-flash_v2_5" ttsLanguage="en-US" welcomeGreeting="Hello &amp; welcome, say &#34;desk&#34; to start." welcomeGreetingInterruptible="speech" interruptible="speech" reportInputDuringAgentSpeech="speech" preemptible="false" dtmfDetection="false"></ConversationRelay>
  </Connect>
  <Hangup></Hangup>
</Response>
